text:
Sam D: heads-up: weird mismatch between Node/CJS and edge/ESM in our SDK sample. edge picks ESM ok at runtime, but TS consumers lose typings and import shape is inconsistent. anyone hit this? :confused:

Ben K: can you paste your package.json exports? likely conditional exports + types not mapped.

Sam D: snippet from failing sample:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```
Edge runtime (Vercel edge) runs fine, but TypeScript projects doing `import Redwood from "redwood-sdk"` see no default and no types. Node consumers on CJS are fine.

Chandra R: likely two things: 1) TS resolver falling back to `exports` semantics (so needs explicit types subpath), 2) CJS bundler interop (default vs named). Do you have `types` field or `types` inside exports?

Sam D: we only had top-level `types": "dist/index.d.ts"`. d.ts exists. weirdly, when the sample runs via the edge bundler, editors in the consumer repo show missing types.

Frank P: edge bundlers and TS `moduleResolution` vary. Add explicit `types` mapping inside `exports` to be safe: 
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "types": "./dist/index.d.ts",
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
  }
}
```
That often fixes type lookup when `exports` is present.

Ben K: also confirm `typesVersions` or a `types` subpath for `./*` if you ship multiple entrypoints. TS's `bundler` resolution can prefer `exports`.

Sam D: tried adding `types` under exports — consumer TS now finds declarations. runtime default shape still off for CJS: `import Redwood from 'redwood-sdk'` becomes `{ default: [Function] }` in some Node envs.

Chandra R: two approaches for parity: 1) publish native ESM and provide a tiny CJS bridge that does `module.exports = require('./dist/esm').default ?? require('./dist/esm')`, or 2) keep CJS main and provide ESM wrapper that re-exports default correctly. Edge-first teams prefer publishing ESM primary.

Frank P: agree. If we go ESM-primary, update publish playbook and add a smoke test that asserts both `require()` and `import` shapes in Node 14/16 and a simulated edge bundler resolution.

Ben K: can we add a simple CI job in samples that runs `node -e "console.log(require('./package').default ? 'd' : 'n')"` and also run a TS compile check with `moduleResolution: bundler`? lightweight but catches regressions.

Sam D: will open a PR to samples/entrypoint-interop with: 1) add `types` to exports, 2) add small cjs wrapper `dist/cjs/index.js` that normalizes default, 3) add tests: node require test + ts compile with bundler resolution, 4) doc note in devex/publish-playbook.md. aiming to send PR today. repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples/entrypoint-interop (branch: edge-types-fix).

DevBot: sample-ci/entrypoint-interop build failed on edge-smoke earlier (logs: https://ci.redwood.dev/12345) :x: flagged failing import shape.

Ben K: also add a CI lint that checks `package.json` exports include `types` when top-level types exists. small script but saves pain.

Chandra R: and add a short note in the SDK README about recommended import patterns for TS consumers (`import Redwood from 'redwood-sdk'` vs `import * as Redwood from 'redwood-sdk'`) plus example for bundlers that treat default differently.

Frank P: I'll add a line in the release checklist to smoke test edge sample on Vercel/Cloudflare pages for each dual-pkg release.

Sam D: thanks all — i'll post PR when ready and tag reviewers. :+1:

Ben K: great, thanks Sam.
